title: Admin Panel — user management, credit grants, dashboard stats
summary: Proceed with create-feature pipeline. F66 is a straightforward CRUD+UI feature with well-established patterns in the codebase. All foundational pieces exist (is_admin, CreditService.grant, JWT auth, FastAPI deps). Risk is low and scope is bounded.

options.name: Full create-feature pipeline (Architect → Waves → TechLead → QA)
options.description: Run the standard 4-agent pipeline. Architect plans tasks for: (1) require_admin FastAPI dependency, (2) admin API router (GET /admin/users, PATCH /admin/users/{id}/credits, GET /admin/dashboard), (3) AdminRoute frontend guard, (4) Admin page with user table + credit grant/revoke, (5) conditional nav for is_admin. Tests and i18n included.
pros: Follows established project workflow — consistency with F22-F65
TechLead review catches edge cases (e.g. admin granting to self, negative balance, pagination)
QA ensures test coverage stays above 91% backend / 90% frontend
ADR for admin authorization pattern is documented
cons: Higher ceremony for a relatively straightforward feature
May take 4 waves when 2 would suffice

options.name: Lightweight implementation — skip Architect, direct Developer+QA
options.description: Since all building blocks exist (is_admin, CreditService, auth deps, existing admin page pattern in AdminLigaStatus), skip the Architect phase and go straight to implementation with a QA pass at the end.
pros: Faster delivery for a well-understood feature
cons: Skips structured task planning — risk of scope creep or missed edge cases
No TechLead review means potential security gaps in admin authorization
Breaks workflow consistency — all prior features used full pipeline

options.name: Defer — admin manages credits via CLI/DB only
options.description: The seed user already has is_admin=1 and 50 credits. Admin could grant credits via a new CLI command (e.g. `cli grant-credits --user-id 2 --amount 10`) without building a full UI.
pros: CLI-only is adequate for single-admin scenario
cons: No visibility into user list or credit balances without DB queries
Does not scale if more users are onboarded
Feature explicitly requests a frontend admin page — would not satisfy requirements

rationale: Option A (full pipeline) is the right choice for three reasons: (1) Admin endpoints are security-sensitive — the TechLead review is valuable for catching authorization bypass, IDOR, and privilege escalation issues. (2) The overhead is modest since all building blocks exist — the Architect will likely produce only 2 waves. (3) Consistency with the project's established workflow ensures documentation (ADR, diagrams, i18n) is not forgotten. Option B saves marginal time but sacrifices the security review. Option C does not satisfy the stated requirements.
preconditions_met: CreditService has grant() and deduct() methods (F65)
JWT auth and get_current_user dependency exist (F22)
AdminLigaStatus page provides frontend admin pattern reference
get_credit_service FastAPI dependency exists in deps.py

risks.risk: Admin privilege escalation — non-admin accessing admin endpoints
risks.mitigation: require_admin dependency must raise 403 before any business logic runs

risks.risk: Admin granting negative credits to drain a user's balance below 0
risks.mitigation: Validate grant amount > 0, use separate revoke action with balance floor check

risks.risk: No audit trail for admin credit operations
risks.mitigation: CreditService already logs CreditTransaction rows — ensure admin grants include admin_user_id in reference_id or reason

next_action: Run /create-feature F66 with the full pipeline
